items.title: Hermes Agent v0.23.4
items.content:
Hermes Agent v0.23.4
Release Date: November 23, 2026

Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~229 PRs merged since v0.23.3 into a stable release for the GitHub release (CLI and installers), the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes for this window ship with v0.24.0.


About this release
Measured at commit 8fc03744473, the window since v0.23.3 contains 1,122 non-merge commits across 1,316 changed files (+96,873 / −6,703), 229 merged PRs and 281 closed issues.
Also in the window, undocumented here on purpose: Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Neon and Carbon on Nous Portal, OpenRouter and Vertex, hermes gateway migrate --backends to move an old serve/dashboard backend onto the gateway (with a System page card in the dashboard), hermes plugins config to edit a plugin's settings from the terminal, approval cards in Desktop for a sandbox's folder and site requests, gateway clients announcing who they are so plugins can see which client sent a turn, a long run of Desktop streaming and transcript performance work, a retryable indicator for slow profile switches, hermes dashboard password without a TTY prompt, configurable skill index description length (skills.index_desc_limit), managed-scope config honored by security and URL-safety reads, and a large batch of new plugin-catalog entries.
Full curated release notes for this window ship with v0.24.0, which will document everything from v0.23.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.
Updating

Microsoft Store app: updates through the Store.
Desktop app installed from the installer (.exe / .dmg): no change in this release; it updates with the next bundled release.
CLI: hermes update, or re-run the installer one-liner.
Docker / Hermes Cloud: nousresearch/hermes-agent:stable (or :latest).

Full Changelog: v0.23.3...v0.23.4

Want Hermes following up your leads this month? Inside the AI Profit Boardroom you get step-by-step video trainings, the Agent OS, a Hermes Agent kit, daily Q&A with me and four live coaching calls a week, with 3,700+ members learning next to you.

The structured paid courses
Udemy: Hermes Agent: Build a Self-Improving AI Agent
Arnold Oberleiter’s Udemy course was last updated in August 2026 and runs 6 hours 27 minutes over 7 sections. It asks for basic AI, API and token knowledge, plus a terminal. You install Hermes on Mac, Linux, Windows through WSL2, a VPS or Docker, then move through Telegram, model switching, browser automation, memory and soul files, skills, cron jobs, voice mode with ElevenLabs, MCP, plugins and hooks. Later lectures reach Hermes Desktop, subagents and Kanban, email and calendar through Zapier MCP, Obsidian, Ollama and RL training with LoRA. A safety section covers prompt injection.
NetworkChuck Academy: Build Your Own Learning AI Worker
NetworkChuck and Jeremy Cioara teach this course in 10 videos across 5 hours. The project is an IT admin agent for a homelab that reports on network, storage and VM status from UniFi, Synology and VMware. You also learn what makes an agent different from a chatbot, installs on Linux, macOS, WSL2, servers and cloud, plus permissions, MCP, APIs and local LLMs. Access comes with a paid Academy membership.
Scrimba on Coursera: Introduction to Hermes Agent
Taught by Maham Codes, this Coursera course is a single module: 11 videos and a quiz, about an hour. It covers how Hermes is built, local or VPS setup, a Telegram bot, skills, memory, choosing a model to manage cost, and upkeep. It sits at intermediate level, comes with Coursera Plus and gives you a shareable certificate.
The free routes: official docs and YouTube
The official Hermes Agent Learning Path
Nous Research keeps a free Learning Path in the Hermes Agent docs. Beginner is about 1 hour: Installation, Quickstart, CLI Usage, Configuration. Intermediate is 2 to 3 hours: Sessions, Messaging, Tools, Skills, Memory, Cron. Advanced takes 4 to 6 hours and covers Architecture, Adding Tools, Creating Skills and Contributing. Goal-based routes sit alongside, for example a Telegram or Discord bot, task automation or model training. Hermes is open source under MIT, with the code on GitHub.
Free YouTube full courses

NeuralNine: a crash course of about 1h17m, from setup through skills, plugins, scheduled tasks and profiles.
Tech With Tim: a full course and setup guide aimed at complete beginners.
Peter Yang: a 45-minute build of an AI chief of staff with Telegram, voice replies, Google Workspace and cron briefings.
Samin Yasar: three hours on multi-agent workflows, dashboards and keeping model costs down.

Free videos are great for a first look. They can’t answer your question when your own setup breaks.
The live option: O’Reilly
Build Your First Local Agent with Hermes is a two-hour, intermediate live event with Lucas Soares. You match a local model (Qwen, Gemma, Llama and similar) to your computer, run Hermes with memory that sticks and skills it writes on its own, and learn when to pick Hermes, Claude Code or OpenClaw. The audience is AI and ML engineers, developers and technical founders.

Ready to hand your first job to Hermes? Join the AI Profit Boardroom → for the step-by-step trainings and four live coaching calls a week.

Join the AI Profit Boardroom →

How to pick: your level and your goal

Complete beginner: Tech With Tim or the docs beginner track first; after that, join the AI Profit Boardroom for someone to look over your setup.
Developer: Udemy for breadth, or the advanced docs track for how Hermes works inside.
IT pro or homelab owner: NetworkChuck Academy.
Business owner: the Boardroom, because each lesson starts from a job like email, outreach or SEO.

Then match your goal. A personal assistant on your phone starts with Peter Yang, then my Hermes Agent Telegram guide. A coding helper starts with the docs coding assistant route. Business automation starts with the Boardroom and my list of best Hermes Agent use cases. RL training starts with the docs training route and Udemy’s RL section.
The learning order that works

Learn the basics. One free video or the docs beginner track, so the words make sense.
Pick one course. Just one, from the table above.
Build one real job. A morning summary on a schedule, or draft replies to your most common customer question.
Get live help. Take what keeps breaking to a coaching call and fix it.

Most people do it the other way round: three courses, zero jobs. Flip it. For the business side, read Hermes Agent for business next.
One course, one running job and real support: that is how you get value from the best Hermes Agent course.
About Julian Goldie
I’m Julian Goldie — founder of Goldie Agency and the AI Profit Boardroom. I test new AI tools and agents almost every day for 428K+ YouTube subscribers, and I run my own business on the same Agent OS I teach. Join the AI Profit Boardroom for the daily builds and live coaching.

The AI Profit Boardroom. It pairs a full Hermes lesson and 60+ newer tutorials with the Agent OS and four live coaching calls a week. For a self-paced course, Udemy comes next.

Give it one job you repeat every week, like a daily summary or reply drafts, and keep approvals on. Add skills one at a time once it runs smoothly.

The structured paid courses

Udemy: Hermes Agent: Build a Self-Improving AI Agent

Arnold Oberleiter’s Udemy course was last updated in August 2026 and runs 6 hours 27 minutes over 7 sections. It asks for basic AI, API and token knowledge, plus a terminal. You install Hermes on Mac, Linux, Windows through WSL2, a VPS or Docker, then move through Telegram, model switching, browser automation, memory and soul files, skills, cron jobs, voice mode with ElevenLabs, MCP, plugins and hooks. Later lectures reach Hermes Desktop, subagents and Kanban, email and calendar through Zapier MCP, Obsidian, Ollama and RL training with LoRA. A safety section covers prompt injection.

NetworkChuck Academy: Build Your Own Learning AI Worker

NetworkChuck and Jeremy Cioara teach this course in 10 videos across 5 hours. The project is an IT admin agent for a homelab that reports on network, storage and VM status from UniFi, Synology and VMware. You also learn what makes an agent different from a chatbot, installs on Linux, macOS, WSL2, servers and cloud, plus permissions, MCP, APIs and local LLMs. Access comes with a paid Academy membership.

Scrimba on Coursera: Introduction to Hermes Agent

Taught by Maham Codes, this Coursera course is a single module: 11 videos and a quiz, about an hour. It covers how Hermes is built, local or VPS setup, a Telegram bot, skills, memory, choosing a model to manage cost, and upkeep. It sits at intermediate level, comes with Coursera Plus and gives you a shareable certificate.

The free routes: official docs and YouTube

The official Hermes Agent Learning Path

Nous Research keeps a free Learning Path in the Hermes Agent docs. Beginner is about 1 hour: Installation, Quickstart, CLI Usage, Configuration. Intermediate is 2 to 3 hours: Sessions, Messaging, Tools, Skills, Memory, Cron. Advanced takes 4 to 6 hours and covers Architecture, Adding Tools, Creating Skills and Contributing. Goal-based routes sit alongside, for example a Telegram or Discord bot, task automation or model training. Hermes is open source under MIT, with the code on GitHub.
